# Claude Code documented contract simulation, snapshot 2026-11-05

This fixture models a small subset of the documentation, not a recorded run, binary-version certification, complete protocol, or supported HUD capability. All identities, paths, content and costs are synthetic. The simulator requires no account or provider CLI. The snapshot is dated; it is **not** pinned to a Claude executable version, because the current official pages are rolling documents. Version-specific items must be rechecked against the target binary.

Sources, accessed 2026-11-05:
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless: `-p`, newline-delimited `stream-json`, partial text deltas and final `result`; default discovery versus `--bare`. Bare skips hooks, including those explicitly passed in settings, and auto-discovered MCP; explicitly supplied `--mcp-config` can still connect. It disables background subagents; the additional-directory skills exception is outside this fixture. Before v2.1.286 some bare-mode runtime restrictions differed; this fixture does not model older releases.
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstart and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstop: documented hook input fields; `SubagentStart` also fires on resume; stop can be an internal agent with empty `agent_type`, and last message is not always a handback report.
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents: native subagents are distinct from a HUD delegation and have their own context. Built-in Explore and Plan are one-shot; this fixture uses the resumable general-purpose agent. The page notes a resume history issue before v2.1.304, but this snapshot is not a claim of testing that binary.

The `stream_event` and `result` records deliberately include only fields needed for these documented facts. An unknown record and arbitrary byte splitting are consumer robustness cases, not claims that the client emits that event or uses those chunk boundaries. Hook input is a separate, test-only side-channel file. It is **not** a Claude transcript. The negative reader test deliberately supplies these records as invalid transcript inputs to check that they do not produce delegation evidence; it does not represent them as official transcript records. The simulator does not claim to implement shell hooks, the trust UI, MCP protocol, custom agent selection, provider auth, resume storage, timing, process teardown, or a real Claude runtime.

Current product integration: the HUD has a transcript reader, not a Claude `stream-json` or hook consumer. A negative test sends these limited partial/result/unknown stream envelopes to that reader solely to check it does not invent a native delegation; this is not an endorsement of that input as a transcript. It does not cover common assistant/user stream envelopes or parent_tool_use_id and does not establish global stream rejection. The known `--bare` configuration-observation coverage gap is not silently promoted by these tests.
